title: Sealed-bid auction with a public reserve price
summary: One item is sold. Every bidder knows its own value and sends one sealed bid; the highest bid at or above the reserve wins and, under the second-price rule, pays the larger of the reserve and the highest other bid.

roles.name: bidder
roles.description: Wants the item and knows what it is worth to them.

steps.name: bidding
steps.description: All bidders send a sealed bid without seeing any other bid.

steps.name: settlement
steps.description: The rule picks the winner and the price, or declares the item unsold.

secrets.what: A bidder's value is known only to that bidder.

payoffs.description: The winner gets its value minus the price; everyone else gets 0.

invariants.name: losers_pay_nothing
invariants.statement: A bidder who does not win pays nothing.

invariants.name: price_at_least_reserve
invariants.statement: If the item is sold, the price is at least the reserve.

assumptions.text: If two bidders tie for the highest bid, the one whose name comes first alphabetically wins.
Under the second-price rule the reserve acts like a bid by the seller: the winner pays the larger of the reserve and the highest other bid.
A bid exactly equal to the reserve can win; bids below the reserve are ignored, and if none clears it the item is unsold and nobody pays.
The reserve, the pricing rule, the tie-break rule and the names of all bidders are shown to every bidder before bidding.
If any bidder sends no bid, the whole run stops; a missing bid is not treated as a bid of zero.
A bidder may bid more than its value and can end with a negative payoff.
After settlement every bidder is told the winner's name and what the winner paid, and its own bid, payment and payoff; other bids are shown only when reveal_bids is on.
